page: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v7 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. It also includes 5669 GB of local storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple compute and memory workloads. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance rank in the top 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with small-block cached reads and large-block writes achieving top-tier results. Cryptographic and compression operations, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, also place in the top 10%. Database operations perform exceptionally well, as demonstrated by a Passmark database score in the top 10% and Redis SET operations reaching 140.26 million operations per second.

From a resource density perspective, the instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial local storage alongside balanced compute and memory resources. However, without dedicated GPU hardware, it is less suited for heavy parallel graphics processing or massive deep learning training, though it maintains strong CPU-based LLM inference speeds for small and medium models. The combination of high-speed AMD EPYC cores, large local storage, and high memory bandwidth makes this server well-suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, data-intensive web serving, and enterprise general-purpose applications.
